observed: The route and page heading identify BTC/PLN.
The headline market price and statistics use PLN.
The converter and the section labelled Price of BTC in PLN use EUR.
The page offers withdrawal of Solana to another crypto wallet.
The same sentence limits external wallets to Bitcoin and Ethereum only.
The SDK converts Retry-After with Number(header) and returns it unchanged.
The SDK README documents retryAfter as milliseconds.
HTTP Retry-After numeric delay is defined in seconds and also permits an HTTP-date.
The developer reference says every API request needs custom Ed25519 headers.
Public endpoint curl examples use an unrelated Bearer token.
The official repository reference says /public endpoints require no authentication.
The developer Node.js example signs /api/1.0/crypto-exchange/orders.
It uses BTC/USD, type, side and qty.
The current contract uses POST /api/1.0/orders, BTC-USD and order_configuration.
Authenticated endpoint examples include timestamp and signature.
They omit X-Revx-API-Key although the same reference marks it required.
The example request is for /public/order-book/BTC-USD.
The example response identifies ETH and Ethereum levels.
Earlier bounded captures showed an empty conversion result for amount or amount-to links.
Later captures of equivalent routes rendered successfully.
A deterministic failure mechanism has not been established.
The official contract explicitly specifies descending order for asks and bids.
Descending asks therefore cannot be reported as an accidental sorting defect without runtime evidence of a different contract.
